title: Instant Pot Hainanese-Style Chicken Rice with Ginger-Scallion Sauce
dek: Skin-on chicken thighs and jasmine rice cook together over a ginger-garlic broth, then meet crisp cucumber and two bright table sauces for a complete family bowl.
image_alt: Hainanese-style sliced poached chicken with golden jasmine rice, cucumber, greens and chile and ginger sauces on a white plate
ingredients: 6 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 2 1/4 lb total)
4 scallions, white and green parts separated and thinly sliced

instructions.name: Season and temper the chicken
instructions.text: Pat the thighs dry and season on both sides with 1 teaspoon salt and the white pepper. Let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes while you rinse the rice until the water is nearly clear, then drain it thoroughly. Wash hands and sanitize surfaces after handling raw chicken.

instructions.name: Brown the skin lightly
instructions.text: Select Sauté on Normal on a 6-quart electric pressure cooker. Add neutral oil and place the thighs skin-side down in two batches. Cook 3 minutes, just until pale gold; transfer to a clean plate. The chicken will not be cooked through.

instructions.name: Deglaze the thin base
instructions.text: Add 1 teaspoon sesame oil, garlic, ginger and the scallion whites; stir for 30 seconds. Cancel Sauté, pour in the broth and scrape the base completely smooth with a wooden spoon. No browned spot should remain.

instructions.name: Layer rice and chicken
instructions.text: Stir the drained rice and 1/2 teaspoon salt into the broth just until level. Set the thighs skin-side up in one layer on top without stirring them into the rice. Keep the pot below the half-full line because rice expands, and do not double this recipe in a 6-quart cooker.

instructions.name: Pressure-cook and release
instructions.text: Lock the lid and cook on High Pressure for 5 minutes; allow 10 to 12 minutes to reach pressure. Let pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then vent any remainder in short controlled pulses. Pause if starchy steam sputters and open only after the float valve drops.

instructions.name: Verify doneness and crisp
instructions.text: Check the thickest part of several thighs, avoiding bone, for 165°F. If any is cooler, return it to the pot on Sauté Low with a splash of broth until safe. For crisper skin, transfer safe chicken to a foil-lined tray and broil 2 to 3 minutes while the rice rests.

instructions.name: Make the two sauces
instructions.text: Mix scallion greens, sugar, remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and remaining 2 teaspoons sesame oil in a heatproof bowl; pour over the 2 tablespoons hot neutral oil. In another bowl, stir soy sauce, lime juice and honey. Keep chile-garlic sauce at the table so the shared meal stays mild.

instructions.name: Build the plates
instructions.text: Fluff the rice and rest it 5 minutes. Slice the chicken from the bones if desired, then serve over rice with cucumber. Spoon on ginger-scallion sauce, drizzle with soy-lime sauce and let diners add chile-garlic sauce themselves.

why_it_works: Rinsed, well-drained jasmine rice absorbs the measured broth while bone-in thighs shield it from direct heat.
Two cups of thin broth and a thoroughly scraped base create steam before rice settles, reducing burn-warning risk.
A ten-minute natural release finishes the rice gently and limits starchy sputtering at the valve.
swaps: Use six boneless skinless thighs and cook for 4 minutes with the same 10-minute natural release; verify 165°F.
Replace cucumber with quickly blanched baby bok choy for a warm vegetable side.
For gluten-free bowls, use certified gluten-free tamari in place of soy sauce.
storage: Remove chicken from the bones, cool chicken and rice in separate shallow containers within 2 hours, and refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat both to 165°F; add 1 tablespoon water per cup of rice before covering. Freeze the chicken and rice separately for up to 2 months. Keep the fresh sauces and cucumber refrigerated for up to 3 days.
notes: Total time includes browning, a 10- to 12-minute pressurizing period, the 5-minute cycle, a 10-minute natural release, optional broiling and resting.
Written for a 6-quart electric pressure cooker. Follow your model manual for minimum liquid, the half-full grain limit, locking and venting; never force the lid.
Do not use converted or brown rice with this timing. Different rice types need different liquid and pressure times.
The base is intentionally mild. Chile-garlic sauce belongs at the table, where each diner controls the heat.

faqs.q: Why did my rice turn soft?
faqs.a: The most common causes are rice that was not drained well, extra liquid from a substituted chicken cut or a release longer than 10 minutes. Measure the broth precisely and fluff after the stated rest.

faqs.q: Can I stack the chicken thighs?
faqs.a: A slight overlap is fine, but a tall pile cooks unevenly and presses into the rice. Use six medium thighs in one loose layer in a 6-quart pot.

faqs.q: Can I make this with chicken breasts?
faqs.a: Breasts are leaner and can dry before the rice finishes. If using them, choose two thick bone-in, skin-on breasts, halve them crosswise and verify every piece reaches 165°F.

title: Instant Pot Greek Beef Stifado with Pearl Onions
dek: Beef chuck, sweet pearl onions, red wine, tomato and warm cinnamon become a glossy Greek-style braise with a deliberate thin-liquid layer and a calm natural release.
image_alt: Greek beef stifado with fork-tender beef chunks and whole pearl onions in a glossy red tomato sauce
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb boneless beef chuck, trimmed and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
12 oz frozen pearl onions, thawed and patted dry
Cooked orzo or crusty bread, for serving
Crushed red pepper, optional for serving

instructions.name: Season the beef
instructions.text: Pat beef dry and toss with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt and black pepper. Keep chilled until the pot is hot, and wash hands and surfaces after contact with raw meat.

instructions.name: Brown the pearl onions
instructions.text: Select Sauté on High on a 6-quart electric pressure cooker. Heat 1 tablespoon oil and cook pearl onions for 5 minutes, turning until spotted brown. Transfer them to a bowl; they finish later without dissolving.

instructions.name: Brown the beef in batches
instructions.text: Add remaining oil and brown beef in three uncrowded batches, about 4 minutes per batch. Transfer each batch to a plate. Browning builds flavor; the centers remain raw.

instructions.name: Build and fully deglaze
instructions.text: Reduce Sauté to Normal. Cook chopped onion 4 minutes, then stir in garlic and tomato paste for 45 seconds. Pour in wine and scrape until the base is completely smooth; simmer 3 minutes. Add broth, 1 tablespoon vinegar, oregano, cinnamon and bay leaves.

instructions.name: Layer for pressure
instructions.text: Return beef and its juices and stir once. Pour crushed tomatoes over the top and do not stir them into the bottom. Lock the lid only after confirming the contents sit below the maximum-fill line.

instructions.name: Pressure-cook and release
instructions.text: Cook on High Pressure for 35 minutes; allow about 15 minutes to reach pressure. Let pressure release naturally for 15 minutes, then vent the remainder in short controlled pulses. Open only after the float valve drops.

instructions.name: Finish the onions and sauce
instructions.text: Remove cinnamon and bay leaves. Stir in browned pearl onions and select Sauté Low for 8 to 10 minutes, until onions are tender and the sauce coats a spoon. Add honey, remaining vinegar and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt to taste.

instructions.name: Verify and serve
instructions.text: Check several beef pieces for at least 145°F followed by a 3-minute rest; for a tender braise they should also yield easily to a fork, commonly near 195 to 205°F. If tough, simmer covered on Sauté Low with a splash of broth. Finish with parsley and offer crushed red pepper at the table.

why_it_works: Wine and broth form a full two cups of thin liquid against the heating plate while crushed tomato stays safely on top.
Browning and pressure tenderize chuck, while pearl onions added after pressure keep their identity and gentle sweetness.
Vinegar added in two stages balances the beefy sauce without making the pressure liquid harsh.
swaps: Replace wine with 1 cup additional beef broth plus 2 teaspoons extra red wine vinegar added after pressure.
Use 1-inch wedges from two medium red onions if pearl onions are unavailable; add them after pressure and simmer until tender.
Serve over mashed potatoes instead of orzo, keeping starches outside the cooker so the pressure liquid stays thin.
storage: Cool in shallow containers within 2 hours. Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat the stew to 165°F on the stovetop, loosening with broth as needed. Store orzo separately so it does not absorb the sauce.
notes: Total time includes batch browning, wine reduction, about 15 minutes to pressurize, the 35-minute cycle, a 15-minute natural release and final simmer.
Written for a 6-quart electric pressure cooker. Follow the exact model manual for minimum liquid, maximum fill and venting, and never force the lid.
Tomato stays on top during pressure cooking. Stirring it down can place thick sauce against the heating plate and trigger a burn warning.
The braise is mild and aromatic. Put crushed red pepper on the table rather than in the shared pot.

faqs.q: Why is my beef safe but still tough?
faqs.a: Safety and tenderness are separate. Beef is safe at 145°F with a three-minute rest, but chuck needs more collagen breakdown. Simmer gently or repressurize for 5 minutes if pieces do not yield to a fork.

faqs.q: Can I use fresh pearl onions?
faqs.a: Yes. Blanch them for 1 minute, slip off the skins, brown as directed and simmer after pressure until a knife slides through the center.

faqs.q: Does the wine cook away completely?
faqs.a: No method guarantees zero alcohol. The open simmer and later cooking reduce it, but use the broth-and-vinegar swap when avoiding alcohol is important.

title: Thai-Style Shrimp Som Tam with Green Papaya & Peanuts
dek: Crisp green papaya, juicy shrimp, long beans, tomatoes and peanuts are gently pounded into a bright lime–fish sauce dressing, with a measured mild base and extra chile for the table.
image_alt: Thai-style shrimp som tam with cooked shrimp, shredded green papaya, tomato, long beans and crushed peanuts in lime dressing
ingredients: 1 small firm green papaya (about 1 1/2 lb), peeled, seeded and julienned to yield 5 cups
8 oz medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
6 oz yardlong beans or green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 small Thai chile, seeded and chopped, plus more for serving
2 tbsp palm sugar or light brown sugar
4 cups cooked sticky rice, optional for serving

instructions.name: Poach and chill the shrimp
instructions.text: Bring 3 cups water and the kosher salt to a bare simmer. Add shrimp and cook 2 to 3 minutes, stirring once, until opaque and 145°F at the thickest part. Drain and spread on a clean plate in the refrigerator while you prepare the salad.

instructions.name: Choose and shred the papaya
instructions.text: Use a hard, fully green, unripe papaya with pale flesh. Peel and halve it, scrape out every seed, then julienne the flesh with a hand guard or shredder. Rinse briefly in cold water and spin very dry.

instructions.name: Pound the aromatic base
instructions.text: In a large mortar, gently pound garlic, the seeded chile and sugar until the garlic breaks down. Add lime juice, fish sauce and tamarind and stir until the sugar dissolves. Start with one chile; place extra at the table.

instructions.name: Bruise the beans and tomatoes
instructions.text: Add beans and pound 5 to 6 times to bruise but not crush them. Add tomatoes and press just until they release some juice. If using a small mortar, make the dressing there and transfer it to a large sturdy bowl.

instructions.name: Dress the papaya
instructions.text: Add papaya and half the peanuts. Use a spoon in one hand and the pestle in the other to lift, turn and lightly pound for 1 to 2 minutes, until strands flex and absorb the dressing without becoming limp.

instructions.name: Fold in shrimp and serve
instructions.text: Taste: it should be distinctly sour and salty with enough sweetness to round the edges. Add lime, fish sauce or sugar 1 teaspoon at a time. Fold in the chilled shrimp without pounding, mound on a platter, scatter over remaining peanuts and serve immediately with sticky rice, lime and extra chile.

why_it_works: Pounding bruises the sturdy papaya surface so dressing clings while the center stays crunchy.
Adding tomato after the aromatics preserves juicy pieces instead of turning the salad watery.
Shrimp is poached only to 145°F, then chilled and folded in last so it stays juicy rather than being crushed.
swaps: For a vegetarian version, replace shrimp with 8 ounces seared firm tofu and use vegan fish sauce or light soy sauce.
If green papaya is unavailable, use 4 cups julienned kohlrabi plus 1 cup julienned carrot; the flavor differs but the crunch and method hold.
Roasted cashews can replace peanuts for a peanut-free version if tree nuts are suitable.
storage: Som tam is crispest immediately. Refrigerate leftovers promptly in a covered container for up to 24 hours; keep at 40°F or below, drain excess liquid and add fresh peanuts before serving. Do not freeze. Keep cooked sticky rice refrigerated separately and reheat until steaming hot.
notes: Green papaya means unripe papaya; ripe orange fruit is too soft and sweet for this salad.
Use a hand guard with any mandoline or julienne slicer, and stop before the papaya piece becomes difficult to hold safely.
Fish sauce is concentrated and salty, so season only after tasting the finished dressing.
Use a clean plate for the cooked shrimp; never return it to packaging or a surface that held it raw.

faqs.q: Can I make som tam without a mortar and pestle?
faqs.a: Yes. Crush garlic and chile with the flat of a knife, whisk the dressing in a sturdy bowl, then squeeze and toss the beans and papaya firmly with a wooden spoon.
Papaya that was not dried, over-pounded tomatoes or a long rest can release excess liquid. Spin the shreds dry and dress only when ready to serve.

faqs.q: Is raw green papaya the same as ripe papaya?
faqs.a: No. Green papaya is firm, pale and neutral, more like a crisp vegetable. A ripe orange papaya will collapse under the pestle and make the dressing too sweet.

title: Syrian-Style Muhammara Roasted Pepper & Walnut Dip
dek: Roasted red peppers, toasted walnuts, crisp breadcrumbs and pomegranate molasses blend into a smoky, tangy dip sturdy enough for pita yet bright enough for a mezze plate.
image_alt: Deep red muhammara roasted pepper and walnut dip drizzled with olive oil beside toasted pita triangles dusted with zaatar
ingredients: 2 jars (12 oz each) roasted red peppers, drained and patted very dry
2 tbsp pomegranate molasses, plus more for serving
1 tsp Aleppo pepper, plus more for serving
1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving

instructions.name: Toast the walnuts
instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F. Spread walnuts on a sheet pan and toast 7 to 9 minutes, until fragrant and one shade darker. Cool completely; reserve 2 tablespoons for garnish.

instructions.name: Dry the peppers
instructions.text: Drain peppers, open them flat and blot both sides thoroughly with clean towels. Excess brine is the main reason muhammara turns loose instead of scoopable.

instructions.name: Build the textured base
instructions.text: Pulse remaining walnuts and breadcrumbs in a food processor 6 to 8 times until coarse, not powdery. Add peppers, pomegranate molasses, lemon, garlic, Aleppo pepper, cumin and salt.

instructions.name: Blend without overworking
instructions.text: Pulse 8 to 10 times, scraping once, until cohesive but still visibly textured. With the machine running, stream in 1/3 cup olive oil. If the blades stall, add water 1 teaspoon at a time, using no more than 1 tablespoon.

instructions.name: Toast the pita
instructions.text: Arrange pita wedges on the walnut pan, brush lightly with a little additional olive oil and sprinkle with zaatar. Bake 5 to 7 minutes at 350°F until crisp at the edges.

instructions.name: Rest and plate
instructions.text: Let the dip stand 10 minutes so breadcrumbs hydrate, then taste for salt, lemon and molasses. Swirl onto a shallow plate and top with reserved walnuts, parsley, a thin olive-oil drizzle and a few drops of pomegranate molasses. Serve with warm pita.

why_it_works: Thoroughly dried peppers and absorptive fresh breadcrumbs create a dip that holds a spooned swirl.
Short pulses preserve walnut texture and prevent the mixture from turning oily or pasty.
Pomegranate molasses supplies concentrated sweet-sour depth without thinning the roasted pepper base.
swaps: Roast three large red bell peppers under the broiler, steam, peel and drain them in place of jarred peppers.
Use gluten-free bread for the crumbs and certified gluten-free crackers instead of pita when needed.
A mix of 2 teaspoons mild red-pepper flakes and 1/4 teaspoon sweet paprika can stand in for Aleppo pepper.
storage: Refrigerate muhammara in an airtight container for up to 5 days; bring it toward room temperature for 20 minutes and stir before serving. Freeze without garnish for up to 2 months, thaw overnight and refresh with lemon and olive oil. Keep toasted pita airtight at room temperature for 2 days.
notes: Walnuts can scorch quickly; pull them when fragrant rather than waiting for a dark color.
Pomegranate molasses varies in sweetness and acidity, so adjust only after the 10-minute rest.
For the texture shown, stop blending while small walnut and pepper flecks remain visible.
This dip contains walnuts and gluten unless you use the noted substitutions.

faqs.a: The peppers probably carried extra brine or the dip was blended too long. Fold in 1 tablespoon fresh breadcrumbs, rest 10 minutes and reassess before adding more.

faqs.q: Can I make it ahead for a party?
faqs.a: Yes. Make it up to three days ahead, but wait to add the garnish and final olive-oil drizzle until serving.

faqs.q: Is muhammara supposed to be smooth?
faqs.a: It should be cohesive and spreadable, but fine walnut and pepper texture is part of its character. A completely silky purée can taste heavy.

title: Belgian Liège Waffles with Caramelized Pearl Sugar
dek: An enriched yeasted dough studded with pearl sugar cooks into dense, tender waffles with deeply caramelized edges and crisp sugar pockets.
image_alt: Close-up of a handheld Belgian Liège waffle with a thick golden grid and deeply caramelized pearl-sugar edges
ingredients: 12 tbsp (170 g) unsalted butter, very soft but not melted
Neutral oil, for the waffle iron
Powdered sugar or berries, optional for serving

instructions.name: Start the yeast mixture
instructions.text: Stir warm milk, yeast and granulated sugar in a stand-mixer bowl. Rest 5 minutes, until creamy at the surface. Whisk in eggs and vanilla.

instructions.name: Develop the dough
instructions.text: Add flour and salt. Mix with the dough hook on low until no dry flour remains, then on medium-low for 5 minutes. Add soft butter 1 tablespoon at a time, waiting until each addition disappears. Continue kneading 6 to 8 minutes, until glossy, elastic and tacky.

instructions.name: Give the dough its first rise
instructions.text: Cover the bowl and let rise in a warm draft-free place for 60 to 75 minutes, until about doubled. If the room is cool, use the oven with only the light switched on; do not heat the oven.

instructions.name: Fold in pearl sugar
instructions.text: Gently deflate the dough and knead in pearl sugar on low speed for 30 to 45 seconds, just until distributed. Divide into eight pieces of about 120 g each and shape loosely into balls.

instructions.name: Rest and preheat
instructions.text: Cover portions and rest 15 minutes. Preheat a Belgian-style waffle iron to medium, about 350–375°F if it has a temperature control. Lightly brush both plates with neutral oil.

instructions.name: Cook in batches
instructions.text: Set one dough ball in each waffle section without pressing it flat. Close and cook 3 to 5 minutes, until deep golden, caramelized and at least 190°F in the bready center. Use silicone-tipped tongs; melted sugar is extremely hot.

instructions.name: Cool briefly and serve
instructions.text: Transfer waffles to a wire rack for 5 minutes so the sugar shell sets. Serve warm and mostly plain, or add a light dusting of powdered sugar and berries.

instructions.name: Clean the iron safely
instructions.text: Unplug the iron and let it cool until warm, not cold. Wipe softened sugar with damp paper towels and a wooden or silicone tool, following the manufacturer's cleaning directions; never immerse an electric waffle iron.

why_it_works: A brioche-like dough, rather than pourable batter, gives Liège waffles their dense, chewy-tender crumb.
Butter added after gluten develops enriches the dough without preventing structure from forming.
Pearl sugar stays in distinct pieces long enough to caramelize against the hot plates.
swaps: If Belgian pearl sugar is unavailable, crush white sugar cubes into 1/4-inch pieces; do not substitute fine Swedish pearl sugar.
Use orange zest in place of vanilla for a citrus variation that does not alter the dough's hydration.
Knead by hand for 12 to 15 minutes before gradually working in butter if you do not have a stand mixer.
storage: Cool completely and store airtight at room temperature for 1 day or refrigerate up to 4 days. Freeze between parchment sheets for up to 2 months. Reheat from chilled or frozen in a 325°F oven for 6 to 10 minutes; a microwave softens the caramelized exterior.
notes: Milk above 120°F can damage yeast; check it with a thermometer rather than guessing.
Pearl sugar caramel gets hotter than ordinary waffle batter. Keep hands clear and let the waffle rest before biting.
A dark nonstick iron may brown faster; begin checking at 3 minutes and lower the heat if sugar smokes.
Do not stack hot waffles. Steam softens the crisp, caramelized ridges.

faqs.q: Why didn't my dough become smooth after adding butter?
faqs.a: The butter may have been added too quickly or was partially melted. Keep mixing on medium-low; a properly developed dough usually gathers and turns glossy within several minutes.

faqs.q: Can I refrigerate the dough overnight?
faqs.a: Yes. Complete the first rise in the refrigerator for 8 to 16 hours. Bring the dough out for 30 minutes, fold in pearl sugar, portion and rest 20 minutes before cooking.

faqs.q: Why are these waffles denser than restaurant Belgian waffles?
faqs.a: Liège waffles are made from enriched yeast dough and are intentionally dense and chewy. Light rectangular Brussels waffles come from a different, pourable batter.
